seo.metaDescription: Horizontal steps from a starting value to a calculated end: what added to it and what took away. Hatched start, solid end, dotted connectors.

props.markdown: A walk from one value to another in horizontal rows: a start, one row per change, and an end that the chart works out for you. Each step is a bar floating between the running total before and after it.

Use `WaterfallChart` to explain a difference: why cash fell over a month, which drivers moved margin between two quarters, what pulls a result under its target. You pass the `start` and the `steps` (signed changes); the end row is the sum, labeled “Total” unless you set `end={{ label }}`. The start is hatched (`startTone`, neutral by default) and the end is solid (`endTone`, accent), so the eye reads “from” and “to”. Dotted connectors link each bar to the next, and `connectors={false}` removes them. `stepLabel` rewrites the text on the right of a step, for example to add the money behind a percentage change. The domain does not force zero, so a small change stays readable; set `domain` to zoom in further.

If you would rather see the running totals as vertical columns, with a cap showing each change and a note under it, use [BridgeChart](/docs/bridge-chart). A waterfall shows the changes, a bridge shows the totals they lead to.

`format` takes a preset, here `currency-compact` with one digit, so every total and the axis share it. `start` and `end` carry your own labels, and the steps mix gains and losses. All props are plain data.

`stepLabel` writes the text on the right of each step from the step itself, here the change in points and the money behind it from `meta`. `domain` zooms in and `connectors={false}` drops the dotted lines. A function prop means this example is a client component.

`WaterfallChart` is built on `Chart`, so it follows the same keyboard model as the other charts: it is a single tab stop, and tabbing in shows the first row with its tooltip and announces it. Arrow keys move to the previous or next row, `Home` and `End` jump to the first and last, `Enter` or `Space` selects the active row when the chart has `onSelect`, and `Esc` clears the active row. `Esc` is only consumed when a row is active, so an enclosing dialog still closes. The widget’s description ends with a keyboard hint (“Use arrow keys to move between points, Home and End for first and last, Escape to clear.”, plus “Press Enter to select.” with `onSelect`); `keyboardHint` replaces it, for example to translate it, and `keyboardHint=""` turns it off.

Screen readers get the chart title and description, then an announcement for each row the keyboard moves to. A step reads “2 of 7, Labor overruns, −1.6 pts · $7.7K, running total 36.4%”: its position, label, the step text (your `stepLabel`, or the signed change in `format`) and the running total after it. The start and end read as “1 of 7, Target, 38.0%”, without a running total. A visually hidden data table with the columns Item, Change and Total follows the chart; `dataTable` renames the caption and headers, or turns it off.
The full model is in the [accessibility guide](https://github.com/mwadon/tally-charts/blob/main/docs/a11y.md).
